# Django Static Files (`django.contrib.staticfiles`): Step-by-Step Guide

Every website needs files that are **not generated by Python**: CSS stylesheets, JavaScript, images, icons, fonts. They are the same for every visitor and never change while the site is running — that's why they are called **static files**. `django.contrib.staticfiles` is Django's built-in app that **finds** these files across your project and apps, **serves** them while you develop, and **collects** them into one folder so a real web server (or WhiteNoise, or a CDN) can serve them in production.

It gives you:

| Part                                             | What it does                                                                                                   |
|--------------------------------------------------|----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| **`{% static %}` template tag**                  | Turns `'blog/style.css'` into the real URL, e.g. `/static/blog/style.css` (or a hashed URL in production)      |
| **`static()` function**                          | The same thing in Python code: `static('blog/style.css')`                                                      |
| **Finders**                                      | Look for static files in every app's `static/` folder and in the folders listed in `STATICFILES_DIRS`          |
| **`runserver` (overridden)**                     | The staticfiles app replaces `runserver` with a version that serves static files automatically when `DEBUG=True` |
| **`collectstatic` command**                      | Copies every static file from every location into one folder: `STATIC_ROOT`                                    |
| **`findstatic` command**                         | Tells you which file on disk a static path resolves to — the #1 debugging tool                                 |
| **Storage backends**                             | Decide where collected files go and what URLs they get: `StaticFilesStorage`, `ManifestStaticFilesStorage`     |
| **`ManifestStaticFilesStorage`**                 | Adds a content hash to every file name (`style.27e20196a850.css`) so browsers can cache files forever          |
| **`staticfiles_storage`**                        | The configured storage object, usable from Python (`staticfiles_storage.url(...)`)                             |
| **`StaticLiveServerTestCase`**                   | A test case that serves static files during live-server (browser) tests                                        |
| **System checks**                                | Warn you about wrong settings (`staticfiles.E001` … `W004`) before anything breaks                             |

Five words you will see a lot:

- **Static file** = a file sent to the browser exactly as it is on disk (CSS, JS, images, fonts). Written by **you**, the developer.
- **Media file** = a file **uploaded by users** (avatars, attachments). Handled by `MEDIA_URL` / `MEDIA_ROOT`, **not** by this app (but explained in Step 22 so you never mix them up).
- **Static path** (or "relative path") = the name you use in code, e.g. `'blog/style.css'`. It is **not** a disk path and **not** a URL.
- **Finder** = a class that knows where to search for a static path on disk.
- **`STATIC_ROOT`** = the single folder `collectstatic` copies everything into, for production.

This guide continues the `blog` project from [django-setup-guide.md](django-setup-guide.md), [django-admin-guide.md](django-admin-guide.md), [django-auth-guide.md](django-auth-guide.md), [django-contenttypes-guide.md](django-contenttypes-guide.md), [django-sessions-guide.md](django-sessions-guide.md) and [django-messages-guide.md](django-messages-guide.md) (project package `config`, apps `blog`, `accounts`, `social` and `usersessions`, `blog/static/blog/style.css` already created in Step 14 of the setup guide). Every step builds on the previous one. Commands are for **Windows** (PowerShell); they are the same on macOS/Linux except where noted.

---

## Prerequisites

- The project from the earlier guides, with the virtual environment **activated** (`(venv)` in your prompt).
- **Django 4.2+** (this guide uses the `STORAGES` setting, added in 4.2). Django 5.x / 6.x recommended. Check with:
  ```bash
  python -m django --version
  ```
- A browser with **Developer Tools** (Chrome, Edge or Firefox — press `F12`). You'll use the **Network** tab to see which files load, their status codes (`200`, `304`, `404`) and their headers.
- If you enabled `LoginRequiredMiddleware` in the auth guide (Step 21): static files served by `runserver` are **not** affected by it (Step 13.4 explains why), so you don't need to change anything for CSS/JS to load on the login page.

---

## Step 0: How Static Files Work (Big Picture)

### 0.1 The problem

A browser loads your page, sees `<link rel="stylesheet" href="/static/blog/style.css">`, and makes a **second request** for `/static/blog/style.css`. Something has to answer that request with the file's bytes. But:

1. Your files are **scattered**: each app has its own `static/` folder, the admin has its own (inside the Django package in `venv\Lib\site-packages`), and you may have a project-wide folder too.
2. Django (Python) is **slow and wasteful** at sending files compared to a dedicated web server (Nginx, IIS, a CDN) — every file request would occupy a Python worker.
3. Browsers **cache** files. When you change `style.css`, visitors with the old copy cached might not see your change.

### 0.2 The solution — three jobs

`django.contrib.staticfiles` solves this with three jobs:

```
                 SOURCE folders (you edit these)
  ┌───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
  │ blog/static/blog/style.css                                    │
  │ accounts/static/accounts/login.css                            │
  │ static/css/base.css               (STATICFILES_DIRS)          │
  │ venv/.../django/contrib/admin/static/admin/css/base.css       │
  └───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
          │                                         │
          │ 1. FIND (finders)                       │ 1. FIND (finders)
          ▼                                         ▼
  2. SERVE IN DEVELOPMENT                 3. COLLECT FOR PRODUCTION
  runserver + DEBUG=True                  python manage.py collectstatic
  answers /static/... directly                      │
  from the source folders                           ▼
                                          staticfiles/   (STATIC_ROOT)
                                          ├── admin/...
                                          ├── blog/style.css
                                          ├── css/base.css
                                          └── accounts/login.css
                                                    │
                                                    ▼
                                          Nginx / IIS / WhiteNoise / CDN
                                          answers /static/... in production
```

And in templates you never hard-code URLs — you write `{% static 'blog/style.css' %}` and Django produces the right URL for the current setup.

### 0.3 The four rules that explain everything

1. **You refer to files by static path** (`'blog/style.css'`), never by disk path or full URL.
2. **The first match wins.** Finders search locations in a fixed order; if two locations contain `style.css` at the same static path, only the first is used. That's why app files live in `static/<app_name>/` (Step 4).
3. **Django serves static files only in development** (`runserver` with `DEBUG=True`). In production, *you* must arrange for something else to serve `STATIC_ROOT`.
4. **`collectstatic` must run on every deploy** — it's the bridge between rules 1–3 and production.

### 0.4 Static vs. media vs. templates

| | **Static files** | **Media files** | **Templates** |
|---|---|---|---|
| Who creates them | You (developer) | Users (uploads) | You (developer) |
| Examples | `style.css`, `app.js`, `logo.svg` | avatars, PDFs, post images | `base.html`, `post_list.html` |
| Sent to browser | As-is | As-is | Rendered by Django first |
| In Git? | Yes (source folders) | No | Yes |
| URL setting | `STATIC_URL` | `MEDIA_URL` | — (rendered by views) |
| Disk setting | `STATIC_ROOT` (collected) | `MEDIA_ROOT` | `TEMPLATES['DIRS']` |
| Handled by | `django.contrib.staticfiles` | `FileField` / default storage | template engine |
| Trusted? | Yes | **No** — never trust uploads | Yes |

## Step 1: Check That Static Files Are Enabled

`startproject` turns static files on for you. Check the two required pieces in `config/settings.py`.

### 1.1 The app in `INSTALLED_APPS`

```python
INSTALLED_APPS = [
    'django.contrib.admin',
    'django.contrib.auth',
    'django.contrib.contenttypes',
    'django.contrib.sessions',
    'django.contrib.messages',
    'django.contrib.staticfiles',   # 👈 this guide
    # ... your apps: 'accounts', 'blog', 'social', 'usersessions'
]
```

The app has **no models and no migrations** — it creates no database tables. Its position in the list only matters for two things:

- **Management commands**: it overrides `runserver`. If another app also overrides `runserver` (e.g. `daphne`, or WhiteNoise's `whitenoise.runserver_nostatic`), the one listed **first** wins — those apps must be placed **above** `django.contrib.staticfiles`.
- **`AppDirectoriesFinder`** searches app `static/` folders in `INSTALLED_APPS` order (Step 8).

### 1.2 `STATIC_URL`

At the bottom of `settings.py`:

```python
# Static files (CSS, JavaScript, Images)
# https://docs.djangoproject.com/en/stable/howto/static-files/

STATIC_URL = 'static/'
```

`STATIC_URL` is the **URL prefix** for all static files. Rules:

- It **must end with a slash** (`'static/'`, not `'static'`).
- A **relative** value (`'static/'`, no leading slash) is automatically prefixed with the site's script prefix — `/static/` normally, `/myblog/static/` if the site is deployed under `/myblog/` (Step 24.2). This is the recommended form.
- An **absolute path** (`'/static/'`) or a **full URL** (`'https://cdn.example.com/static/'`) are also allowed.
- It **must be different** from `MEDIA_URL`.

### 1.3 Verify

Open the Django shell:

```bash
python manage.py shell
```

```python
>>> from django.apps import apps
>>> apps.is_installed('django.contrib.staticfiles')
True
>>> from django.conf import settings
>>> settings.STATIC_URL            # note: the leading slash was added for you
'/static/'
>>> print(settings.STATIC_ROOT)    # not set yet — Step 14
None
>>> settings.STATICFILES_DIRS      # empty yet — Step 7
[]
>>> settings.STATICFILES_FINDERS   # the defaults
['django.contrib.staticfiles.finders.FileSystemFinder', 'django.contrib.staticfiles.finders.AppDirectoriesFinder']
>>> exit()
```

List the commands the app adds:

```bash
python manage.py help
```

You'll see a section:

```
[staticfiles]
    collectstatic
    findstatic
    runserver
```

Run the system checks:

```bash
python manage.py check
```

```
System check identified no issues (0 silenced).
```

### 1.4 What happens if something is missing

| Missing / wrong                                  | Symptom                                                                                                                          |
|--------------------------------------------------|----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| `django.contrib.staticfiles` not installed       | `{% static %}` still prints URLs, but `runserver` returns **404** for them; the admin looks unstyled; `collectstatic` → `Unknown command: 'collectstatic'` |
| `STATIC_URL` missing or `None`                   | `ImproperlyConfigured: You're using the staticfiles app without having set the required STATIC_URL setting.`                     |
| `STATIC_URL` without trailing slash              | `ImproperlyConfigured: ... STATIC_URL setting must end with a slash.`                                                             |
| `STATIC_URL == MEDIA_URL`                        | `ImproperlyConfigured: The MEDIA_URL and STATIC_URL settings must have different values`                                          |
| `STATIC_ROOT` missing when running `collectstatic` | `ImproperlyConfigured: You're using the staticfiles app without having set the STATIC_ROOT setting to a filesystem path.`       |
| `DEBUG = False` with `runserver`                 | Every static file → **404** (by design — Step 13.3)                                                                               |

---

## Step 2: Know What the App Contains

`django.contrib.staticfiles` lives in `venv\Lib\site-packages\django\contrib\staticfiles\`. Each module has one job:

| Module                                   | Contains                                                                                       | You use it for                                  |
|------------------------------------------|------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|-------------------------------------------------|
| `apps.py`                                | `StaticFilesConfig` (label `staticfiles`, `ignore_patterns = ['CVS', '.*', '*~']`)             | Changing ignore patterns (Step 14.8)            |
| `checks.py`                              | System checks for `STATICFILES_DIRS`, `STORAGES`                                               | Runs automatically with `check` / `runserver`   |
| `finders.py`                             | `FileSystemFinder`, `AppDirectoriesFinder`, `DefaultStorageFinder`, `BaseFinder`, `find()`     | Locating files (Steps 8, 10)                    |
| `storage.py`                             | `StaticFilesStorage`, `ManifestStaticFilesStorage`, `ManifestFilesMixin`, `HashedFilesMixin`, `staticfiles_storage` | Where files go and their URLs (Steps 15–17) |
| `handlers.py`                            | `StaticFilesHandler` (WSGI), `ASGIStaticFilesHandler` (ASGI)                                   | What `runserver` uses to serve files            |
| `views.py`                               | `serve(request, path, insecure=False)`                                                         | Serving through a URL pattern (Step 13.5)       |
| `urls.py`                                | `staticfiles_urlpatterns()`                                                                    | Same                                            |
| `testing.py`                             | `StaticLiveServerTestCase`                                                                     | Browser tests (Step 25.5)                       |
| `utils.py`                               | `get_files()`, `matches_patterns()`, `check_settings()`                                        | Writing custom finders / storages               |
| `management/commands/collectstatic.py`   | The `collectstatic` command                                                                    | Step 14                                         |
| `management/commands/findstatic.py`      | The `findstatic` command                                                                       | Step 9                                          |
| `management/commands/runserver.py`       | `runserver` that wraps the app in `StaticFilesHandler`                                         | Step 13                                         |

The **`{% static %}` tag and `static()` function** are not in this folder — they live in `django/templatetags/static.py`. They work even without the app, but when the app **is** installed they ask `staticfiles_storage` for the URL (which is what makes hashed URLs possible).

---

## Step 3: Your First Static File (Revisited)

In the setup guide you created `blog/static/blog/style.css`. Let's understand every piece, then add more files.

### 3.1 The folders

```
blog/
└── static/          ← AppDirectoriesFinder looks for a folder with exactly this name
    └── blog/        ← namespace folder = the app name (Step 4 explains why)
        ├── style.css
        ├── images/
        │   └── logo.svg
        └── js/
            └── post.js
```

Create the new folders (PowerShell):

```powershell
New-Item -ItemType Directory -Force blog\static\blog\images
New-Item -ItemType Directory -Force blog\static\blog\js
```

(macOS/Linux: `mkdir -p blog/static/blog/images blog/static/blog/js`)

### 3.2 Add files

`blog/static/blog/images/logo.svg`:

```xml
<svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="40" height="40" viewBox="0 0 40 40">
  <rect width="40" height="40" rx="8" fill="#0c4b33"/>
  <text x="20" y="27" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="20" fill="#fff" text-anchor="middle">B</text>
</svg>
```

`blog/static/blog/js/post.js`:

```javascript
// Runs on every page that includes it. Proves the JS file loaded.
document.addEventListener('DOMContentLoaded', () => {
    console.log('blog/js/post.js loaded');
});
```

Add to `blog/static/blog/style.css` (keep what's already there):

```css
.site-header {
    display: flex;
    align-items: center;
    gap: 12px;
}

.site-header img {
    width: 40px;
    height: 40px;
}
```

### 3.3 Use them in `base.html`

`blog/templates/blog/base.html` (head and header part):

```html
{% load static %}
<!DOCTYPE html>
<html lang="en">
<head>
    <meta charset="UTF-8">
    <meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1">
    <title>{% block title %}My Blog{% endblock %}</title>
    <link rel="stylesheet" href="{% static 'blog/style.css' %}">
    <script src="{% static 'blog/js/post.js' %}" defer></script>
</head>
<body>
    <header class="site-header">
        <img src="{% static 'blog/images/logo.svg' %}" alt="My Blog logo">
        <a href="{% url 'blog:post_list' %}">My Blog</a>
    </header>
    {% block content %}{% endblock %}
</body>
</html>
```

### 3.4 Try it

```bash
python manage.py runserver
```

1. Open **http://127.0.0.1:8000/** — the logo shows and the styles apply.
2. **View the page source** (`Ctrl+U`). The tags became plain URLs:
   ```html
   <link rel="stylesheet" href="/static/blog/style.css">
   <script src="/static/blog/js/post.js" defer></script>
   <img src="/static/blog/images/logo.svg" alt="My Blog logo">
   ```
3. Open **http://127.0.0.1:8000/static/blog/style.css** directly — you see the raw CSS.
4. Look at the terminal running `runserver`. Each file is a separate request:
   ```
   "GET / HTTP/1.1" 200 1534
   "GET /static/blog/style.css HTTP/1.1" 200 412
   "GET /static/blog/js/post.js HTTP/1.1" 200 142
   "GET /static/blog/images/logo.svg HTTP/1.1" 200 298
   ```
5. Press `F5` again: you'll see **`304`** instead of `200` — "Not Modified". The browser asked "has it changed since last time?" and Django said no, so no bytes were re-sent (Step 13.6).
6. Open DevTools → **Console**: `blog/js/post.js loaded`.

### 3.5 The URL → file mapping

```
URL:          http://127.0.0.1:8000/static/blog/images/logo.svg
                                  └──┬──┘└──────────┬─────────┘
                                STATIC_URL     static path
                                               'blog/images/logo.svg'
                                                     │ finders search for it
                                                     ▼
Disk:         C:\...\myproject\blog\static\blog\images\logo.svg
                               └─┬─┘└──┬──┘└──────────┬──────┘
                               app   'static'    static path
```

**Important:** the app's own `static/` folder is **not** part of the static path. `blog/static/blog/style.css` has the static path `blog/style.css` — the second `blog` is the namespace you created.

### 3.6 New `static/` folders need a server restart

The finders build their list of folders **when the server starts**. If you create a `static/` folder in an app that didn't have one (or add a new `STATICFILES_DIRS` entry), **restart `runserver`** — otherwise you get 404s for the new files. New *files* in an already-known folder are picked up immediately.

---

## Step 4: Why `static/blog/` and Not Just `static/` (Namespacing)

### 4.1 The collision

All app `static/` folders are merged into **one** namespace. Suppose you did *not* namespace:

```
blog/static/style.css         → static path 'style.css'
accounts/static/style.css     → static path 'style.css'   ← same path!
```

`{% static 'style.css' %}` can only point to **one** of them — the first one found (the app listed higher in `INSTALLED_APPS`). The other is silently ignored, and `collectstatic` prints:

```
Found another file with the destination path 'style.css'. It will be ignored since only the first encountered file is collected. If this is not what you want, make sure every static file has a unique path.
```

### 4.2 Prove it

```powershell
New-Item -ItemType Directory -Force accounts\static
Set-Content -Encoding utf8 accounts\static\demo.css "/* accounts version */"
New-Item -ItemType Directory -Force blog\static
Set-Content -Encoding utf8 blog\static\demo.css "/* blog version */"
```

Restart `runserver` (new folder for `accounts`) and open **http://127.0.0.1:8000/static/demo.css**. You get the version from whichever app is listed first in `INSTALLED_APPS` (`accounts` if it's above `blog`). Ask Django which ones exist:

```bash
python manage.py findstatic demo.css
```

```
Found 'demo.css' here:
  C:\Users\...\myproject\accounts\static\demo.css
  C:\Users\...\myproject\blog\static\demo.css
```

Two results — the **first** is the one that's used. Clean up:

```powershell
Remove-Item accounts\static\demo.css, blog\static\demo.css
```

### 4.3 The rule

**Always put app static files in `<app>/static/<app>/`**, and reference them as `'<app>/...'`:

```
accounts/static/accounts/login.css     → {% static 'accounts/login.css' %}
blog/static/blog/style.css             → {% static 'blog/style.css' %}
```

Django's own apps follow this: the admin's files are `admin/css/base.css`, `admin/js/core.js`, etc. (Step 12).

---

## Step 5: The `{% static %}` Template Tag — Every Detail

### 5.1 Load it in **every** template that uses it

```html
{% load static %}
```

`{% load %}` is **not inherited**: if `post_detail.html` extends `base.html` and uses `{% static %}` in its own blocks, `post_detail.html` needs its own `{% load static %}` too. Forget it and you get:

```
TemplateSyntaxError: Invalid block tag on line 5: 'static'. Did you forget to register or load this tag?
```

In a child template, `{% extends %}` must be the first tag, so put `{% load static %}` right after it:

```html
{% extends 'blog/base.html' %}
{% load static %}

{% block content %}
    <img src="{% static 'blog/images/logo.svg' %}" alt="">
{% endblock %}
```

### 5.2 Basic usage

```html
<link rel="stylesheet" href="{% static 'blog/style.css' %}">
<link rel="stylesheet" href="{% static "blog/style.css" %}">   {# double quotes work too #}
```

Rules for the path:

- **No leading slash.** Write `'blog/style.css'`, not `'/blog/style.css'`. A leading slash may appear to work in development but can break in production with `ManifestStaticFilesStorage` (missing manifest entry).
- **Forward slashes**, even on Windows (`'blog/images/logo.svg'`, never `'blog\images\logo.svg'`).
- **Case matters** in production (Linux servers and S3 are case-sensitive, even though Windows isn't). `Logo.svg` ≠ `logo.svg`.
- Special characters are URL-encoded for you: `{% static 'blog/my file.pdf' %}` → `/static/blog/my%20file.pdf`. Still, avoid spaces in file names.

### 5.3 Save the URL in a variable — `as`

```html
{% static 'blog/images/logo.svg' as logo_url %}
<img src="{{ logo_url }}" alt="Logo">
<meta property="og:image" content="{{ request.scheme }}://{{ request.get_host }}{{ logo_url }}">
```

The variable is available until the end of the current block.

### 5.4 Use a variable as the path

The path can be any template variable or expression:

```html
{# in the view: context = {'theme': 'dark'} #}
{% with 'blog/themes/'|add:theme|add:'.css' as theme_css %}
    <link rel="stylesheet" href="{% static theme_css %}">
{% endwith %}
```

Never build a static path from **user input** without validating it against a fixed list of allowed values.

### 5.5 `{% get_static_prefix %}` and `{% get_media_prefix %}`

Also from the `static` library:

```html
{% load static %}
{% get_static_prefix %}                  {# prints /static/ #}
{% get_static_prefix as STATIC_PREFIX %}
{% get_media_prefix %}                   {# prints MEDIA_URL, e.g. /media/ #}
```

⚠️ Avoid building file URLs like `{{ STATIC_PREFIX }}blog/style.css`: it skips the storage, so you **lose hashed URLs** in production (Step 16). Use `{% static %}` for files.

### 5.6 The `static` context processor — `{{ STATIC_URL }}`

Add `'django.template.context_processors.static'` to `TEMPLATES[0]['OPTIONS']['context_processors']` and every template gets `{{ STATIC_URL }}`. Same warning as above — it's just the prefix, not a real file URL. It's **not** enabled by default and you rarely need it.

### 5.7 Skip `{% load static %}` everywhere — `builtins`

To make `{% static %}` available in all templates without loading it:

```python
TEMPLATES = [
    {
        'BACKEND': 'django.template.backends.django.DjangoTemplates',
        'DIRS': [BASE_DIR / 'templates'],
        'APP_DIRS': True,
        'OPTIONS': {
            'context_processors': [
                # ... unchanged ...
            ],
            'builtins': ['django.templatetags.static'],   # 👈
        },
    },
]
```

Trade-off: templates become less portable (a reusable app's templates should still `{% load static %}`). Explicit `{% load static %}` is the common convention; this guide keeps it.

### 5.8 What the tag actually does

```
{% static 'blog/style.css' %}
        │
        ▼
staticfiles installed?  ── no ──►  urljoin(STATIC_URL, 'blog/style.css')
        │ yes
        ▼
staticfiles_storage.url('blog/style.css')
        │
        ├── StaticFilesStorage          → '/static/blog/style.css'
        └── ManifestStaticFilesStorage  → DEBUG=True:  '/static/blog/style.css'
                                          DEBUG=False: '/static/blog/style.27e20196a850.css'
```

The tag **never checks the file exists** in development — a typo gives a URL that 404s. In production with `ManifestStaticFilesStorage`, a typo raises an error (Step 16.6).

### 5.9 Never hard-code `/static/`

```html
❌ <link rel="stylesheet" href="/static/blog/style.css">
✅ <link rel="stylesheet" href="{% static 'blog/style.css' %}">
```

Hard-coded URLs break when you change `STATIC_URL` (e.g. to a CDN), deploy under a sub-path, or switch on hashed file names.

### 5.10 Jinja2 templates

If you use Jinja2 (the messages guide, Step 4.7), expose `static` in your environment:

```python
# config/jinja2.py
from django.templatetags.static import static
from jinja2 import Environment


def environment(**options):
    env = Environment(**options)
    env.globals.update({'static': static})
    return env
```

```html
<link rel="stylesheet" href="{{ static('blog/style.css') }}">
```

---

## Step 6: Images, Favicons, Fonts, CSS and JavaScript in Practice

### 6.1 Images

```html
{% load static %}
<img src="{% static 'blog/images/logo.svg' %}" alt="My Blog logo" width="40" height="40">

<picture>
    <source srcset="{% static 'blog/images/hero.webp' %}" type="image/webp">
    <img src="{% static 'blog/images/hero.jpg' %}" alt="">
</picture>
```

Always add `width`/`height` (prevents layout shift) and `alt` text (accessibility; use `alt=""` for decorative images).

### 6.2 Favicon

Browsers request `/favicon.ico` automatically. Point them to a static file instead, in `base.html`'s `<head>`:

```html
<link rel="icon" href="{% static 'favicon.svg' %}" type="image/svg+xml">
<link rel="icon" href="{% static 'favicon.ico' %}" sizes="any">
<link rel="apple-touch-icon" href="{% static 'apple-touch-icon.png' %}">
```

These are site-wide, so they go in the project-level `static/` folder (Step 7). Pages without the `<link>` (the admin, JSON error pages) still make browsers request `/favicon.ico` — you'll see `"GET /favicon.ico HTTP/1.1" 404` in the log. It's harmless; to silence it, add a redirect in `config/urls.py`:

```python
from django.templatetags.static import static
from django.views.generic.base import RedirectView

urlpatterns = [
    # ...
    path('favicon.ico', RedirectView.as_view(url=static('favicon.ico'), permanent=True)),
]
```

### 6.3 CSS: reference other files with **relative** URLs

CSS files are **not** Django templates — `{% static %}` doesn't work inside them. Use paths **relative to the CSS file's own location**:

```
static/
├── css/
│   └── base.css        ← this file
├── fonts/
│   └── inter.woff2
└── images/
    └── pattern.svg
```

```css
/* static/css/base.css */
@font-face {
    font-family: "Inter";
    src: url("../fonts/inter.woff2") format("woff2");
    font-display: swap;
}

body {
    font-family: "Inter", Arial, sans-serif;
    background-image: url("../images/pattern.svg");
}
```

Relative URLs work everywhere: in development, after `collectstatic`, behind a CDN, and `ManifestStaticFilesStorage` rewrites them to hashed names automatically (Step 16.4). **Don't** write `url("/static/images/pattern.svg")` — it breaks if `STATIC_URL` changes.

### 6.4 JavaScript files

```html
<script src="{% static 'blog/js/post.js' %}" defer></script>          {# classic script, runs after HTML is parsed #}
<script type="module" src="{% static 'js/app.js' %}"></script>        {# ES module (deferred automatically) #}
```

Use `defer` (or `type="module"`) so scripts don't block page rendering. Inside ES modules, import with **relative** paths:

```javascript
// static/js/app.js
import { formatDate } from './utils.js';
```

### 6.5 Give JavaScript a static URL

JavaScript files aren't templates either. Three ways to pass a URL from the template to JS:

**a) `data-` attribute (recommended):**

```html
<body data-spinner-url="{% static 'blog/images/spinner.svg' %}">
```

```javascript
const spinnerUrl = document.body.dataset.spinnerUrl;
```

**b) `json_script` (safe for any value):**

```html
{% static 'blog/images/spinner.svg' as spinner_url %}
{{ spinner_url|json_script:"spinner-url" }}
```

```javascript
const spinnerUrl = JSON.parse(document.getElementById('spinner-url').textContent);
```

**c) Inline script (works, but conflicts with a strict Content-Security-Policy):**

```html
<script>
    const SPINNER_URL = "{% static 'blog/images/spinner.svg' %}";
</script>
```

### 6.6 PDFs and other downloads

```html
<a href="{% static 'blog/docs/style-guide.pdf' %}" download>Download the style guide</a>
```

If the file should only be available to logged-in users, it is **not** a static file — static files are public (Step 26). Serve it through a view instead.

---

## Step 7: Project-Level Static Files — `STATICFILES_DIRS`

### 7.1 Why

Some files don't belong to any app: the site-wide stylesheet, the favicon, fonts, a vendored library. Put them in a project-level folder and tell Django about it.

### 7.2 Create the folder and files

```powershell
New-Item -ItemType Directory -Force static\css, static\images, static\fonts, static\js
```

`static/css/base.css` — the CSS from Step 6.3.

`static/images/pattern.svg`:

```xml
<svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="24" height="24">
  <circle cx="2" cy="2" r="1" fill="#e5e5e5"/>
</svg>
```

`static/favicon.svg`:

```xml
<svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 32 32">
  <rect width="32" height="32" rx="6" fill="#0c4b33"/>
  <text x="16" y="22" font-family="Arial" font-size="16" fill="#fff" text-anchor="middle">B</text>
</svg>
```

`static/fonts/inter.woff2` — download Inter (or any font) as `.woff2` from its official site, or remove the `@font-face` rule if you don't want a custom font.

### 7.3 The setting

```python
STATIC_URL = 'static/'

STATICFILES_DIRS = [
    BASE_DIR / 'static',
]
```

- It's a **list** (or tuple) of folders. Use absolute paths — `BASE_DIR / 'static'` is absolute because `BASE_DIR` is.
- Folders are searched **in order**, and **before** app folders (because `FileSystemFinder` comes first in `STATICFILES_FINDERS`). So a file here overrides an app's file with the same static path — useful for overriding third-party apps (Step 12.3).
- The folder **name** doesn't matter (`static`, `assets`, `frontend/dist`…). Files directly inside it have static paths relative to it: `static/css/base.css` → `'css/base.css'`.

Restart `runserver`, then update `base.html`:

```html
{% load static %}
<!DOCTYPE html>
<html lang="en">
<head>
    <meta charset="UTF-8">
    <meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1">
    <title>{% block title %}My Blog{% endblock %}</title>
    <link rel="icon" href="{% static 'favicon.svg' %}" type="image/svg+xml">
    <link rel="stylesheet" href="{% static 'css/base.css' %}">     {# project-wide #}
    <link rel="stylesheet" href="{% static 'blog/style.css' %}">   {# app-specific, loaded after so it can override #}
    {% block extra_css %}{% endblock %}
    <script src="{% static 'blog/js/post.js' %}" defer></script>
    {% block extra_js %}{% endblock %}
</head>
```

Child templates can now add page-specific files:

```html
{% extends 'blog/base.html' %}
{% load static %}

{% block extra_css %}
    <link rel="stylesheet" href="{% static 'blog/post_detail.css' %}">
{% endblock %}
```

### 7.4 Prefixes — `(prefix, path)` tuples

An entry can be a 2-tuple `(prefix, folder)`. Files from that folder get the prefix in their static path:

```python
STATICFILES_DIRS = [
    BASE_DIR / 'static',
    ('downloads', BASE_DIR / 'downloads'),
]
```

```
downloads/brochure.pdf   → static path 'downloads/brochure.pdf'
                         → URL /static/downloads/brochure.pdf
                         → collected to staticfiles/downloads/brochure.pdf
```

The prefix **must not end with a slash** (`'downloads'`, not `'downloads/'`) — otherwise check `staticfiles.E003`.

A common use is exposing just one folder of an npm package, without exposing all of `node_modules`:

```python
STATICFILES_DIRS = [
    BASE_DIR / 'static',
    ('vendor/htmx', BASE_DIR / 'node_modules' / 'htmx.org' / 'dist'),
]
```

```html
<script src="{% static 'vendor/htmx/htmx.min.js' %}" defer></script>
```

### 7.5 System checks for this setting

| Check              | Message                                                                                  | Cause / fix                                                                                     |
|--------------------|------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| `staticfiles.E001` | The STATICFILES_DIRS setting is not a tuple or list. HINT: Perhaps you forgot a trailing comma? | You wrote `STATICFILES_DIRS = (BASE_DIR / 'static')` — that's not a tuple. Use `[...]` or add a comma. |
| `staticfiles.E002` | The STATICFILES_DIRS setting should not contain the STATIC_ROOT setting.                 | `STATIC_ROOT` must be a **different** folder (Step 14.2).                                        |
| `staticfiles.E003` | The prefix 'downloads/' in the STATICFILES_DIRS setting must not end with a slash.        | Remove the trailing slash from the prefix.                                                      |
| `staticfiles.W004` | The directory '...\static' in the STATICFILES_DIRS setting does not exist.               | Create the folder or fix the path. (Warning, not error — `runserver` still starts.)             |

Try E001 — temporarily write:

```python
STATICFILES_DIRS = (BASE_DIR / 'static')
```

```bash
python manage.py check
```

```
SystemCheckError: System check identified some issues:

ERRORS:
?: (staticfiles.E001) The STATICFILES_DIRS setting is not a tuple or list.
	HINT: Perhaps you forgot a trailing comma?
```

Change it back to a list.

### 7.6 App folder or project folder?

| Put it in…                    | When                                                                               |
|-------------------------------|------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| `<app>/static/<app>/`         | The file is used only by that app's templates, or the app may be reused elsewhere  |
| `static/` (`STATICFILES_DIRS`)| Site-wide: base layout CSS, favicon, fonts, vendored libraries, overrides           |

---

## Step 8: Finders — How Django Looks for a File

### 8.1 The setting

```python
# These are the defaults — you don't need to write this unless you change it.
STATICFILES_FINDERS = [
    'django.contrib.staticfiles.finders.FileSystemFinder',      # 1. STATICFILES_DIRS
    'django.contrib.staticfiles.finders.AppDirectoriesFinder',  # 2. <app>/static/
]
```

### 8.2 The search order, exactly

For the static path `'blog/style.css'`:

```
1. FileSystemFinder — each folder in STATICFILES_DIRS, in order:
     C:\...\myproject\static\blog\style.css                          not found
2. AppDirectoriesFinder — each app in INSTALLED_APPS, in order, that HAS a static/ folder:
     ...\django\contrib\admin\static\blog\style.css                  not found
     C:\...\myproject\accounts\static\blog\style.css                 not found
     C:\...\myproject\blog\static\blog\style.css                     ✅ FOUND — stop
```

(Apps without a `static/` folder — `auth`, `sessions`, etc. — are skipped. That list is built when the server starts: Step 3.6.)

### 8.3 The three built-in finders

| Finder                    | Searches                                                                   | On by default |
|---------------------------|----------------------------------------------------------------------------|---------------|
| `FileSystemFinder`        | Every folder in `STATICFILES_DIRS`                                         | ✅            |
| `AppDirectoriesFinder`    | The `static/` subfolder of every installed app                             | ✅            |
| `DefaultStorageFinder`    | The **default file storage** (`STORAGES['default']`, i.e. `MEDIA_ROOT`)    | ❌            |

**Don't** enable `DefaultStorageFinder` with user uploads in `MEDIA_ROOT` — it would let `collectstatic` copy user uploads into your static files. It exists for special cases where static files are stored in the default storage.

### 8.4 Remove a finder

If your project keeps **all** static files in `STATICFILES_DIRS` you could drop `AppDirectoriesFinder` — but then the **admin's** files (and every third-party app's files) are no longer found. In practice, keep both.

### 8.5 Write your own finder

A finder is a class with `find()` (used by `findstatic` and by `runserver`) and `list()` (used by `collectstatic`). Example: look in `themes/<ACTIVE_THEME>/static/` so you can switch site themes with one setting.

```python
# config/finders.py
from django.conf import settings
from django.contrib.staticfiles import utils
from django.contrib.staticfiles.finders import BaseFinder
from django.core.checks import Warning
from django.core.files.storage import FileSystemStorage


class ThemeFinder(BaseFinder):
    """Find static files in themes/<ACTIVE_THEME>/static/."""

    def __init__(self, *args, **kwargs):
        self.location = settings.BASE_DIR / 'themes' / settings.ACTIVE_THEME / 'static'
        self.storage = FileSystemStorage(location=self.location)
        super().__init__(*args, **kwargs)

    def check(self, **kwargs):
        if not self.location.is_dir():
            return [Warning(f'Theme folder {self.location} does not exist.', id='config.W001')]
        return []

    def find(self, path, find_all=False, **kwargs):
        # Django < 5.2 passes the argument as all=...
        find_all = find_all or kwargs.get('all', False)
        full_path = self.location / path
        if full_path.is_file():
            return [str(full_path)] if find_all else str(full_path)
        return [] if find_all else None

    def list(self, ignore_patterns):
        if self.location.is_dir():
            for path in utils.get_files(self.storage, ignore_patterns):
                yield path, self.storage
```

```python
# config/settings.py
ACTIVE_THEME = 'default'

STATICFILES_FINDERS = [
    'config.finders.ThemeFinder',                               # theme files win
    'django.contrib.staticfiles.finders.FileSystemFinder',
    'django.contrib.staticfiles.finders.AppDirectoriesFinder',
]
```

`list()` must yield `(static_path, storage)` pairs; `collectstatic` reads each file from that storage. The `check()` method is run by `manage.py check`.

---

## Step 9: Debug with `findstatic`

`findstatic` runs the finders exactly like `runserver` does and prints the result. **Whenever a static file 404s, run this first.**

### 9.1 Basic

```bash
python manage.py findstatic blog/style.css
```

```
Found 'blog/style.css' here:
  C:\Users\...\myproject\blog\static\blog\style.css
```

Several paths at once:

```bash
python manage.py findstatic blog/style.css css/base.css admin/css/base.css
```

### 9.2 Not found

```bash
python manage.py findstatic blog/styles.css
```

```
No matching file found for 'blog/styles.css'.
```

(Typo: `styles` vs `style`.)

### 9.3 See every location searched — `-v 2`

```bash
python manage.py findstatic blog/style.css -v 2
```

```
Found 'blog/style.css' here:
  C:\Users\...\myproject\blog\static\blog\style.css

Looking in the following locations:
  C:\Users\...\myproject\static
  C:\Users\...\myproject\venv\Lib\site-packages\django\contrib\admin\static
  C:\Users\...\myproject\blog\static
```

If the folder you expected isn't in this list: the app isn't in `INSTALLED_APPS`, the folder isn't named exactly `static`, or the `STATICFILES_DIRS` path is wrong.

### 9.4 All matches vs. first match — `--first`

By default `findstatic` shows **all** matching files (first = the one used). `--first` shows only the winner:

```bash
python manage.py findstatic admin/css/base.css --first
```

### 9.5 Options summary

| Option          | Effect                                                    |
|-----------------|-----------------------------------------------------------|
| `--first`       | Show only the first match (the one actually served)       |
| `-v 0`          | Print only the paths (good for scripts)                   |
| `-v 1`          | Default output                                            |
| `-v 2`          | Also list every location searched                         |

---

## Step 10: Static Files in Python Code

### 10.1 `static()` — get a URL

```python
from django.templatetags.static import static

static('blog/style.css')          # '/static/blog/style.css'  (hashed in production with Manifest storage)
```

Use it in views, JSON APIs, model methods, emails, `RedirectView` (Step 6.2):

```python
# blog/views.py
from django.http import JsonResponse
from django.templatetags.static import static


def app_config(request):
    return JsonResponse({
        'logoUrl': static('blog/images/logo.svg'),
        'spinnerUrl': static('blog/images/spinner.svg'),
    })
```

⚠️ Two different functions are both named `static`:

| Import                                           | What it is                                                         |
|--------------------------------------------------|--------------------------------------------------------------------|
| `from django.templatetags.static import static`  | Returns a **URL** for a static path (this step)                    |
| `from django.conf.urls.static import static`     | Returns **URL patterns** for serving files in dev (media, Step 22) |

If you need both in one file, alias one: `from django.conf.urls.static import static as static_urls`.

### 10.2 `staticfiles_storage` — the storage object

```python
from django.contrib.staticfiles.storage import staticfiles_storage

staticfiles_storage.url('blog/style.css')       # same as static()
staticfiles_storage.exists('blog/style.css')    # looks in STATIC_ROOT — False until you run collectstatic!
staticfiles_storage.path('blog/style.css')      # disk path inside STATIC_ROOT
with staticfiles_storage.open('blog/style.css') as f:
    css = f.read()
```

`staticfiles_storage` works on the **collected** files in `STATIC_ROOT`, not on your source folders. Before `collectstatic`, use the finders instead.

### 10.3 `finders.find()` — get the source file on disk

```python
from django.contrib.staticfiles import finders

finders.find('blog/style.css')
# 'C:\\Users\\...\\myproject\\blog\\static\\blog\\style.css'

finders.find('blog/missing.css')
# None

finders.find('admin/css/base.css', find_all=True)    # Django 5.2+; older versions: all=True
# ['C:\\...\\venv\\Lib\\site-packages\\django\\contrib\\admin\\static\\admin\\css\\base.css']

finders.searched_locations      # folders searched by the last find() call
```

Typical use: embed a file's content, e.g. inline an SVG icon or read a JSON file shipped as a static file:

```python
# blog/templatetags/svg_tags.py
from django import template
from django.contrib.staticfiles import finders
from django.utils.safestring import mark_safe

register = template.Library()


@register.simple_tag
def inline_svg(path):
    """Insert the contents of a static SVG file (our own files only — never user uploads)."""
    full_path = finders.find(path)
    if full_path is None:
        return ''
    with open(full_path, encoding='utf-8') as f:
        return mark_safe(f.read())
```

```html
{% load svg_tags %}
{% inline_svg 'blog/images/logo.svg' %}
```

(Create `blog/templatetags/__init__.py` if the folder doesn't exist yet.) `finders` search source folders, which exist in development; in production they exist too, as long as your code is deployed with its `static/` folders (it normally is).

---

## Step 11: Static Files for Forms and Widgets — `Media`

Forms and widgets can declare the CSS/JS they need. Django then gives you exactly the right `<link>`/`<script>` tags.

### 11.1 A widget with its own assets

```python
# blog/widgets.py
from django import forms


class MarkdownTextarea(forms.Textarea):
    class Media:
        css = {
            'all': ['blog/widgets/markdown.css'],
        }
        js = ['blog/widgets/markdown.js']
```

```python
# blog/forms.py
from django import forms

from .models import Post
from .widgets import MarkdownTextarea


class PostForm(forms.ModelForm):
    class Meta:
        model = Post
        fields = ['title', 'content']
        widgets = {'content': MarkdownTextarea}
```

Create `blog/static/blog/widgets/markdown.css` and `markdown.js` (any content).

### 11.2 Render the media in the template

```html
{% block extra_css %}{{ form.media.css }}{% endblock %}
{% block extra_js %}{{ form.media.js }}{% endblock %}

{% block content %}
    <form method="post">
        {% csrf_token %}
        {{ form }}
        <button type="submit">Save</button>
    </form>
{% endblock %}
```

Output:

```html
<link href="/static/blog/widgets/markdown.css" media="all" rel="stylesheet">
<script src="/static/blog/widgets/markdown.js"></script>
```

`{{ form.media }}` prints both at once. Rules:

- Relative paths (`'blog/widgets/markdown.js'`) go through `static()` — so they get hashed names in production.
- Paths starting with `http://`, `https://` or `/` are used as-is.
- Media from several widgets is **merged** and **de-duplicated** (`form1.media + form2.media` also works).
- The `css` keys are media types: `'all'`, `'screen'`, `'print'`, or `'screen, print'`.
- Django 5.2+: `django.forms.Script('blog/widgets/markdown.js', type='module')` lets you add attributes to a script tag in `Media.js`.

### 11.3 Admin `Media`

Same mechanism in the admin (see the admin guide):

```python
# blog/admin.py
@admin.register(Post)
class PostAdmin(admin.ModelAdmin):
    # ...
    class Media:
        css = {'all': ['blog/admin/post_admin.css']}
        js = ['blog/admin/post_admin.js']
```

These are added to the admin's add/change pages for `Post`.

---

## Step 12: The Admin's Static Files

### 12.1 Where they come from

The admin's CSS, JS and icons are inside the Django package:

```
venv\Lib\site-packages\django\contrib\admin\static\admin\
├── css\    base.css, login.css, forms.css, dark_mode.css, ...
├── img\    icons (SVG)
└── js\     core.js, actions.js, SelectFilter2.js, vendor\jquery\...
```

`AppDirectoriesFinder` finds them because `django.contrib.admin` is installed. In development they "just work"; in production they must be collected and served like your own files — **unstyled admin in production = static files not served** (Step 18).

### 12.2 Add your own admin styles (recommended way)

Create `static/css/admin.css`:

```css
:root {
    --primary: #0c4b33;
    --secondary: #44b78b;
    --header-bg: #0c4b33;
}
```

Create `templates/admin/base_site.html` (you may already have it from the admin guide — just add the `extrastyle` block):

```html
{% extends "admin/base.html" %}
{% load static %}

{% block extrastyle %}
    {{ block.super }}
    <link rel="stylesheet" href="{% static 'css/admin.css' %}">
{% endblock %}
```

The admin uses CSS variables, so overriding a few of them recolours the whole admin.

### 12.3 Override an admin file completely (use rarely)

Because `FileSystemFinder` searches `STATICFILES_DIRS` **before** app folders, a file at the same static path wins:

```
static/admin/img/icon-yes.svg    ← yours, wins
...\django\contrib\admin\static\admin\img\icon-yes.svg   ← ignored
```

Check which one is used:

```bash
python manage.py findstatic admin/img/icon-yes.svg
```

(The first line listed is yours.) Overriding whole files like `admin/css/base.css` is fragile — Django updates may change them. Prefer Step 12.2.

---

## Step 13: Serving Static Files in Development — Every Detail

### 13.1 How `runserver` serves them

When `django.contrib.staticfiles` is installed, `python manage.py runserver` is **its** version of the command. It wraps your project in `StaticFilesHandler`:

```
Request /static/blog/style.css
   │
   ▼
StaticFilesHandler: does the path start with STATIC_URL?
   ├── yes → finders.find('blog/style.css') → send the file (or 404)       ← Django middleware NOT run
   └── no  → normal Django: middleware → URL resolver → view
```

This only happens when **`DEBUG = True`** (or with `--insecure`, Step 13.3). And only when `STATIC_URL` is a local path — if it's a full URL (`https://cdn...`), `runserver` doesn't serve anything.

### 13.2 `--nostatic` — turn it off

```bash
python manage.py runserver --nostatic
```

Static requests now go to your URL patterns like any other request (and 404, unless you added `staticfiles_urlpatterns()`, Step 13.5, or use WhiteNoise, Step 19).

### 13.3 `DEBUG = False` and `--insecure`

Set `DEBUG = False` (with `ALLOWED_HOSTS = ['127.0.0.1', 'localhost']`) and run `runserver`: the page loads **without any CSS**, and the log shows:

```
"GET /static/blog/style.css HTTP/1.1" 404 179
```

That's deliberate: serving files through Python is "grossly inefficient and probably insecure", so Django refuses when `DEBUG` is off. To force it anyway (local testing only):

```bash
python manage.py runserver --insecure
```

Note: `--insecure` still serves from your **source** folders through the finders, not from `STATIC_ROOT`. With `ManifestStaticFilesStorage` the hashed URLs (`style.27e20196a850.css`) don't exist in source folders, so they **404**. To test a production-like setup locally, use WhiteNoise (Step 19.6).

Set `DEBUG = True` again when you're done.

### 13.4 Static files skip middleware

`StaticFilesHandler` answers **before** Django's middleware runs. Consequences:

- `LoginRequiredMiddleware` (auth guide) doesn't block CSS/JS on the login page. ✅
- Middleware-added headers (`SecurityMiddleware`'s `X-Content-Type-Options`, your custom headers) are **not** on static responses in development.
- Static requests don't touch sessions, messages, or the database.

### 13.5 Serving without `runserver` — `staticfiles_urlpatterns()`

If you run the project in development with another server (e.g. `waitress-serve` or `uvicorn`) while `DEBUG = True`, add the static view to your URLs:

```python
# config/urls.py
from django.contrib.staticfiles.urls import staticfiles_urlpatterns

urlpatterns = [
    # ...
]

urlpatterns += staticfiles_urlpatterns()
```

- It returns `[]` when `DEBUG = False`, so it's harmless in production (and useless there).
- It uses `django.contrib.staticfiles.views.serve`, a normal view — so it **does** go through middleware. With `LoginRequiredMiddleware`, anonymous users would be redirected away from CSS files. Prefer `runserver` or WhiteNoise.

The view itself:

```python
from django.contrib.staticfiles.views import serve
# serve(request, path, insecure=False)
#   - DEBUG False and insecure False → Http404
#   - path not found by finders → Http404("'blog/x.css' could not be found")
#   - path is a directory → Http404("Directory indexes are not allowed here.")
```

### 13.6 Browser caching during development

Development responses include `Last-Modified`. The browser re-validates with `If-Modified-Since`, and gets `304 Not Modified` when the file hasn't changed. If you still see an old CSS version:

- **Hard refresh**: `Ctrl+F5` (or `Ctrl+Shift+R`).
- DevTools → Network → tick **Disable cache** (works while DevTools is open).
- Check you edited the file that's actually served (`findstatic`, Step 9 — maybe another file with the same path wins).

### 13.7 ASGI servers in development

- **Daphne**: put `'daphne'` at the **top** of `INSTALLED_APPS`; its `runserver` serves static files like Django's does.
- **Uvicorn**: doesn't serve Django static files. For development only, wrap the app:
  ```python
  # config/asgi.py
  import os

  from django.core.asgi import get_asgi_application

  os.environ.setdefault('DJANGO_SETTINGS_MODULE', 'config.settings')
  application = get_asgi_application()

  from django.conf import settings  # noqa: E402

  if settings.DEBUG:
      from django.contrib.staticfiles.handlers import ASGIStaticFilesHandler
      application = ASGIStaticFilesHandler(application)
  ```
  In production use WhiteNoise or a web server instead.

### 13.8 Windows: CSS/JS served with the wrong MIME type

On some Windows machines, the registry maps `.js` (or `.css`) to `text/plain`. Django uses Python's `mimetypes` module, which reads the registry, so the browser receives `Content-Type: text/plain` and refuses the file:

```
Refused to apply style from 'http://127.0.0.1:8000/static/blog/style.css' because its MIME type ('text/plain') is not a supported stylesheet MIME type, and strict MIME checking is enabled.
```

Check in DevTools → Network → click the file → **Response Headers** → `Content-Type`. Fix in `config/settings.py`:

```python
import mimetypes

mimetypes.add_type('text/javascript', '.js', True)
mimetypes.add_type('text/css', '.css', True)
```

---

## Step 14: `STATIC_ROOT` and `collectstatic` — Every Detail

### 14.1 Why collect?

In production the web server needs **one** folder to serve `/static/` from. Your files are in many places (project `static/`, every app's `static/`, the admin inside `venv`). `collectstatic` copies them all into one folder.

### 14.2 Set `STATIC_ROOT`

```python
STATIC_URL = 'static/'
STATIC_ROOT = BASE_DIR / 'staticfiles'      # 👈 where collectstatic copies to
STATICFILES_DIRS = [BASE_DIR / 'static']    # where YOUR project files live
```

Rules:

- **Absolute path**, to a folder that is **only** for collected files. `collectstatic --clear` deletes everything inside it.
- **Not** a folder in `STATICFILES_DIRS` (error `staticfiles.E002`) — otherwise it would collect into its own source.
- **Not** an app's `static/` folder.
- **Not** `BASE_DIR` itself, or any folder with your code — your web server will make the whole folder public.
- **Different from `MEDIA_ROOT`**.
- The name `staticfiles` is just a convention.

### 14.3 Run it

```bash
python manage.py collectstatic
```

First run (folder doesn't exist / is empty) — no question asked:

```
134 static files copied to 'C:\Users\...\myproject\staticfiles'.
```

(The exact number depends on your Django version and files — most are the admin's.)

Look at the result:

```
staticfiles/
├── admin/
│   ├── css/  img/  js/          ← from the admin app inside venv
├── blog/
│   ├── style.css
│   ├── images/logo.svg
│   └── js/post.js
├── css/
│   └── base.css                 ← from STATICFILES_DIRS
├── favicon.svg
├── fonts/
└── images/
```

The folder structure is exactly the **static paths**. So `/static/blog/style.css` → `staticfiles/blog/style.css` — that's why a web server can serve it directly.

### 14.4 Run it again

```bash
python manage.py collectstatic
```

Now the folder is not empty, so Django asks:

```
You have requested to collect static files at the destination
location as specified in your settings:

    C:\Users\...\myproject\staticfiles

This will overwrite existing files!
Are you sure you want to do this?

Type 'yes' to continue, or 'no' to cancel: yes

0 static files copied to 'C:\Users\...\myproject\staticfiles', 134 unmodified.
```

`collectstatic` compares **modification times**: a file is copied only if the source is newer than the copy. Edit `blog/static/blog/style.css`, run it again: `1 static file copied ..., 133 unmodified.`

### 14.5 Every option

| Option                     | Short | Effect                                                                                                  |
|----------------------------|-------|---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| `--noinput` / `--no-input` |       | Don't ask "Are you sure?" — **use in deploy scripts**                                                   |
| `--clear`                  | `-c`  | Delete **everything** in `STATIC_ROOT` first, then copy. Removes files you deleted from source           |
| `--dry-run`                | `-n`  | Show what would happen, change nothing                                                                  |
| `--link`                   | `-l`  | Create **symbolic links** instead of copies                                                              |
| `--ignore PATTERN`         | `-i`  | Skip files/folders matching a glob pattern; repeatable                                                  |
| `--no-default-ignore`      |       | Don't apply the default ignore patterns (`CVS`, `.*`, `*~`)                                              |
| `--no-post-process`        |       | Skip the storage's post-processing (e.g. no hashing with `ManifestStaticFilesStorage`)                   |
| `-v 0` / `-v 1` / `-v 2` / `-v 3` |  | Verbosity: `0` silent, `1` summary (default), `2` every file copied/skipped                       |

### 14.6 Try each option

**See every file — `-v 2`:**

```bash
python manage.py collectstatic --noinput -v 2
```

```
Skipping 'admin/css/base.css' (not modified)
...
Copying 'C:\Users\...\myproject\blog\static\blog\style.css'
...
1 static file copied to 'C:\Users\...\myproject\staticfiles', 133 unmodified.
```

**Dry run:**

```bash
python manage.py collectstatic --noinput --dry-run
```

```
Pretending to copy 'C:\Users\...\myproject\blog\static\blog\style.css'
...
134 static files copied.
```

**Clear (start fresh):**

```bash
python manage.py collectstatic --noinput --clear
```

The prompt (without `--noinput`) changes to *"This will DELETE ALL FILES in this location!"*. Use `--clear` when you **renamed or deleted** source files — otherwise the old copies stay in `STATIC_ROOT` forever (and stay public).

**Ignore files:**

```bash
python manage.py collectstatic --noinput --ignore "*.scss" --ignore "*.map" --ignore "src"
```

Patterns are matched against file and folder **names** and against the static path.

**Symlinks (`--link`):** saves disk space and makes source changes appear instantly. On **Windows**, creating symlinks needs **Developer Mode** turned on or an Administrator terminal; otherwise you get `OSError: [WinError 1314] A required privilege is not held by the client`. Rarely worth it on Windows.

### 14.7 The default ignore patterns

By default `collectstatic` skips:

| Pattern | Skips                                                                 |
|---------|-----------------------------------------------------------------------|
| `CVS`   | CVS version-control folders                                           |
| `.*`    | Hidden files and folders: `.gitkeep`, `.DS_Store`, `.env`, `.git`     |
| `*~`    | Editor backup files (`style.css~`)                                    |

The `.*` rule is a safety net — a stray `.env` inside a static folder won't become public. Don't use `--no-default-ignore` unless you know you need dotfiles.

### 14.8 Change the default ignore patterns permanently

Subclass the app config:

```python
# config/apps.py
from django.contrib.staticfiles.apps import StaticFilesConfig


class MyStaticFilesConfig(StaticFilesConfig):
    ignore_patterns = [*StaticFilesConfig.ignore_patterns, '*.scss', '*.map', 'src']
```

Replace the app in `INSTALLED_APPS`:

```python
INSTALLED_APPS = [
    # ...
    # 'django.contrib.staticfiles',
    'config.apps.MyStaticFilesConfig',
    # ...
]
```

Now `collectstatic` skips Sass sources and source maps by default. (`findstatic` and `runserver` still serve them.)

### 14.9 Duplicate paths

If two locations have a file with the same static path, `collectstatic` copies the **first** found (same order as Step 8.2) and prints:

```
Found another file with the destination path 'blog/style.css'. It will be ignored since only the first encountered file is collected. If this is not what you want, make sure every static file has a unique path.
```

Treat this as a warning to fix — unless you intentionally overrode a file (Step 12.3).

### 14.10 File permissions

Collected files get the permissions from `FILE_UPLOAD_PERMISSIONS` (default `0o644` — owner read/write, everyone read) and folders from `FILE_UPLOAD_DIRECTORY_PERMISSIONS` (default: system default). On Linux servers these matter (the web server user must be able to **read** the files); on Windows they're mostly ignored. To set them only for static files, use a custom storage (Step 17.2).

### 14.11 Don't commit `staticfiles/`

Add to `.gitignore`:

```
staticfiles/
```

It's generated output — like a build folder. Generate it on the server (or in CI) during deploy.

### 14.12 When to run it

| Situation                                    | Run `collectstatic`?                                           |
|----------------------------------------------|----------------------------------------------------------------|
| Developing with `runserver`, `DEBUG = True`  | **No** — files are served from source folders                   |
| Every deploy to production                   | **Yes**, with `--noinput` (and `--clear` if files were removed) |
| After upgrading Django or a third-party app  | **Yes** — their static files may have changed                   |
| Testing WhiteNoise / production settings locally | **Yes**                                                     |

---

## Step 15: Storage Backends — Overview and the `STORAGES` Setting

### 15.1 What a storage does

The **staticfiles storage** decides two things:

1. **Where** `collectstatic` writes files (local folder, S3 bucket, …).
2. **Which URL** `{% static %}` returns for a static path.

### 15.2 The setting

`STORAGES` (Django 4.2+) configures **all** storages by alias. Two aliases are special: `"default"` (for `FileField` uploads / media) and `"staticfiles"`:

```python
# These are the defaults.
STORAGES = {
    'default': {
        'BACKEND': 'django.core.files.storage.FileSystemStorage',
    },
    'staticfiles': {
        'BACKEND': 'django.contrib.staticfiles.storage.StaticFilesStorage',
    },
}
```

⚠️ If you define `STORAGES` at all, **define both keys**. Defining only `'staticfiles'` removes `'default'`, and file uploads break. (Recent Django versions also report `staticfiles.E005` if `'staticfiles'` is missing.)

Each entry can have `OPTIONS`, passed to the backend's constructor:

```python
'staticfiles': {
    'BACKEND': 'django.contrib.staticfiles.storage.StaticFilesStorage',
    'OPTIONS': {
        'location': BASE_DIR / 'staticfiles',     # overrides STATIC_ROOT
        'base_url': '/static/',                   # overrides STATIC_URL
    },
},
```

(Usually you leave `OPTIONS` out and set `STATIC_ROOT` / `STATIC_URL`.)

### 15.3 Old tutorials: `STATICFILES_STORAGE`

Before Django 4.2 the setting was:

```python
STATICFILES_STORAGE = 'django.contrib.staticfiles.storage.ManifestStaticFilesStorage'   # ❌ removed in Django 5.1
```

It was deprecated in 4.2 and **removed in 5.1**. Translate it to `STORAGES['staticfiles']['BACKEND']`. Similarly, `CachedStaticFilesStorage` was removed in Django 3.1 — use `ManifestStaticFilesStorage`.

### 15.4 The built-in backends

| Backend                                | URL for `'blog/style.css'`                       | Use for                                    |
|----------------------------------------|--------------------------------------------------|--------------------------------------------|
| `StaticFilesStorage` (default)         | `/static/blog/style.css`                         | Development; simple deployments            |
| `ManifestStaticFilesStorage`           | `/static/blog/style.27e20196a850.css` (`DEBUG=False`) | **Production** (cache busting)        |

Third-party:

| Backend                                                      | Package           | Adds                                          |
|--------------------------------------------------------------|-------------------|-----------------------------------------------|
| `whitenoise.storage.CompressedManifestStaticFilesStorage`    | `whitenoise`      | Hashing + `.gz` / `.br` compressed copies     |
| `whitenoise.storage.CompressedStaticFilesStorage`            | `whitenoise`      | Compression only                              |
| `storages.backends.s3.S3Storage`                             | `django-storages` | Upload to Amazon S3 (or compatible)           |
| `storages.backends.s3.S3ManifestStaticStorage`               | `django-storages` | S3 + hashing                                  |

### 15.5 Which storage is active?

```bash
python manage.py shell
```

```python
>>> from django.conf import settings
>>> settings.STORAGES['staticfiles']['BACKEND']
'django.contrib.staticfiles.storage.StaticFilesStorage'
>>> from django.contrib.staticfiles.storage import staticfiles_storage
>>> staticfiles_storage.base_url
'/static/'
>>> staticfiles_storage.location
'C:\\Users\\...\\myproject\\staticfiles'
>>> type(staticfiles_storage)            # a lazy wrapper...
<class 'django.contrib.staticfiles.storage.ConfiguredStorage'>
>>> staticfiles_storage.__class__        # ...around the real storage
<class 'django.contrib.staticfiles.storage.StaticFilesStorage'>
```

---

## Step 16: `ManifestStaticFilesStorage` in Detail

### 16.1 The caching problem

For speed you want browsers to cache CSS/JS for a **long** time (a year). But then, when you deploy a new `style.css`, visitors keep using the old cached one. The fix is **cache busting**: give every *version* of a file a different URL. If the file name contains a hash of its content, a changed file automatically gets a new name, and the old name can be cached forever.

```
style.css   (content A)  →  style.27e20196a850.css
style.css   (content B)  →  style.9f3c2a1b7d44.css     ← new URL, browsers fetch it fresh
```

### 16.2 Turn it on

```python
STORAGES = {
    'default': {
        'BACKEND': 'django.core.files.storage.FileSystemStorage',
    },
    'staticfiles': {
        'BACKEND': 'django.contrib.staticfiles.storage.ManifestStaticFilesStorage',
    },
}
```

Run:

```bash
python manage.py collectstatic --noinput --clear
```

```
134 static files copied to 'C:\Users\...\myproject\staticfiles', 134 post-processed.
```

### 16.3 What it wrote

```
staticfiles/
├── blog/
│   ├── style.css                    ← original copy (still there)
│   ├── style.27e20196a850.css       ← hashed copy
│   └── images/
│       ├── logo.svg
│       └── logo.6a1e3c0d9b52.svg
├── css/
│   ├── base.css
│   └── base.4c8d1f2e0a77.css
└── staticfiles.json                 ← the manifest
```

- The hash = first **12 hex characters of the MD5** of the file content.
- Both the original and the hashed file are kept.
- `staticfiles.json` maps every static path to its hashed name:

```json
{
  "paths": {
    "blog/style.css": "blog/style.27e20196a850.css",
    "blog/images/logo.svg": "blog/images/logo.6a1e3c0d9b52.svg",
    "css/base.css": "css/base.4c8d1f2e0a77.css"
  },
  "version": "1.1",
  "hash": "a3f9c1e07b2d"
}
```

(The `hash` key — a hash of the whole manifest — exists since Django 4.2.)

### 16.4 Post-processing: references inside CSS (and JS) are rewritten

The hashed CSS file has its `url()` references replaced with hashed names too:

```css
/* staticfiles/css/base.4c8d1f2e0a77.css */
@font-face {
    font-family: "Inter";
    src: url("../fonts/inter.5b2e9a1c3d40.woff2") format("woff2");
}
body {
    background-image: url("../images/pattern.e1d0c7b6a593.svg");
}
```

What's rewritten:

| File type | Pattern rewritten                                                                  |
|-----------|------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| CSS       | `url(...)`, `@import "..."`, `/*# sourceMappingURL=... */`                         |
| JS        | `//# sourceMappingURL=...`                                                         |
| JS modules| `import ... from "..."`, `export ... from "..."` — **only if** you enable `support_js_module_import_aggregation` (Step 17.1) |

What's left alone: absolute URLs (`https://...`, `//cdn...`), `data:` URIs, `#fragment`-only references.

This is why Step 6.3 says to use **relative** URLs in CSS.

Because file A can reference file B which references file C, post-processing runs several passes (`max_post_process_passes = 5`). Circular references (A imports B, B imports A) exceed this and fail with `Max post-process passes exceeded.`

### 16.5 `DEBUG` decides which URL you get

```python
>>> from django.templatetags.static import static
>>> static('blog/style.css')
```

| `DEBUG` | Result                                   | Needs `collectstatic`? |
|---------|------------------------------------------|------------------------|
| `True`  | `'/static/blog/style.css'`               | No                     |
| `False` | `'/static/blog/style.27e20196a850.css'`  | **Yes** — URL comes from `staticfiles.json` |

So development keeps working without collecting; production requires it.

### 16.6 Missing manifest entries — `manifest_strict`

With `DEBUG = False`, if a template references a path that's **not in the manifest**, the page crashes with **500**:

```
ValueError: Missing staticfiles manifest entry for 'blog/styles.css'
```

Causes:

1. **Typo** in `{% static %}` — good, you found a bug before your users did.
2. You **forgot to run `collectstatic`** after adding the file (or never ran it).
3. The path has a **leading slash** (`'/blog/style.css'`).
4. You're running **tests** (always `DEBUG = False`) — Step 25.3.

`manifest_strict = True` (the default) is what raises the error. With `manifest_strict = False` (custom subclass, Step 17.1), Django tries to compute the hash from the file in `STATIC_ROOT` instead — which still fails if the file isn't there. Keep it strict and fix the cause.

### 16.7 Post-processing errors during `collectstatic`

If a CSS file references a file that **doesn't exist**, `collectstatic` stops:

```
Post-processing 'css/base.css' failed!

ValueError: The file 'fonts/inter.woff2' could not be found with <django.contrib.staticfiles.storage.ManifestStaticFilesStorage object at 0x...>.
```

Very common with vendored libraries whose minified CSS ends with `/*# sourceMappingURL=bootstrap.min.css.map */` but you didn't copy the `.map` file. Fixes:

- Copy the missing file (e.g. the `.map`) next to the CSS, **or**
- Remove the comment / bad reference from the CSS, **or**
- Fix the relative path (`../fonts/` vs `fonts/`).

`collectstatic --no-post-process` skips hashing completely — useful to confirm the cause, but don't deploy that with `ManifestStaticFilesStorage` (the manifest won't be written, every page 500s).

### 16.8 Other attributes

| Attribute                               | Default               | Meaning                                                                       |
|-----------------------------------------|-----------------------|-------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| `manifest_name`                         | `'staticfiles.json'`  | File name of the manifest in `STATIC_ROOT`                                    |
| `manifest_strict`                       | `True`                | Raise `ValueError` for paths missing from the manifest                        |
| `max_post_process_passes`               | `5`                   | Passes to resolve nested references                                           |
| `keep_intermediate_files`               | `False`               | Keep hashed versions produced by intermediate passes                          |
| `support_js_module_import_aggregation`  | `False`               | Rewrite `import`/`export ... from` in JS (experimental)                       |
| `manifest_hash`                         | —                     | Hash of the manifest (Django 4.2+), e.g. to version a service worker cache    |

Methods you may override: `file_hash(name, content=None)` (how the hash is computed), `hashed_name(name, content=None, filename=None)`, `url(name, force=False)` (`force=True` returns the hashed URL even when `DEBUG = True`). Constructor option `manifest_storage=` (Django 4.2+) stores the manifest in a different storage.

### 16.9 Deploy order matters

```
1. upload new code          (templates reference new hashed names via the NEW manifest)
2. collectstatic --noinput  (writes new hashed files + new staticfiles.json)
3. restart app server       (the manifest is read when the storage is first used — restart to load the new one)
```

Old hashed files stay in `STATIC_ROOT` (unless `--clear`), so pages already open in browsers keep working during the deploy.

---

## Step 17: Custom Static Storages

### 17.1 Tweak `ManifestStaticFilesStorage`

```python
# config/storage.py
from django.contrib.staticfiles.storage import ManifestStaticFilesStorage


class BlogManifestStaticFilesStorage(ManifestStaticFilesStorage):
    # Rewrite `import ... from './utils.js'` in ES modules to hashed names.
    support_js_module_import_aggregation = True
```

```python
STORAGES = {
    'default': {'BACKEND': 'django.core.files.storage.FileSystemStorage'},
    'staticfiles': {'BACKEND': 'config.storage.BlogManifestStaticFilesStorage'},
}
```

Without this setting, JS module imports still work in production (the **unhashed** originals are in `STATIC_ROOT` too), you just don't get cache busting for the imported files.

### 17.2 Set file permissions for collected files only

```python
# config/storage.py
from django.contrib.staticfiles.storage import ManifestStaticFilesStorage


class BlogManifestStaticFilesStorage(ManifestStaticFilesStorage):
    support_js_module_import_aggregation = True

    def __init__(self, *args, **kwargs):
        kwargs.setdefault('file_permissions_mode', 0o644)
        kwargs.setdefault('directory_permissions_mode', 0o755)
        super().__init__(*args, **kwargs)
```

### 17.3 Shorter or different hashes

```python
import hashlib

from django.contrib.staticfiles.storage import ManifestStaticFilesStorage


class Sha256ManifestStaticFilesStorage(ManifestStaticFilesStorage):
    def file_hash(self, name, content=None):
        if content is None:
            return None
        hasher = hashlib.sha256()
        for chunk in content.chunks():
            hasher.update(chunk)
        return hasher.hexdigest()[:16]
```

(Changing the hash scheme changes every URL — browsers download everything once more.)

---

## Step 18: Serving Static Files in Production — Your Options

Once `DEBUG = False`, Django stops serving static files. Pick **one** of these:

| Option                           | How it works                                                     | Good for                                         |
|----------------------------------|------------------------------------------------------------------|--------------------------------------------------|
| **WhiteNoise** (Step 19)         | Python middleware serves `STATIC_ROOT` efficiently, with caching headers and compression | Most projects; PaaS (Render, Railway, Heroku); **Windows + Waitress** |
| **Web server** (Step 20)         | Nginx / Apache / IIS serves `STATIC_ROOT` directly, Django never sees the request | Your own Linux/Windows server                    |
| **CDN / cloud storage** (Step 21)| `collectstatic` uploads to S3 (etc.); `STATIC_URL` points at the CDN | High traffic, global users                       |

All three need: `STATIC_ROOT` set, `collectstatic` run on every deploy, and (recommended) hashed file names.

---

## Step 19: WhiteNoise — Step by Step

### 19.1 Install

```bash
pip install whitenoise
pip freeze > requirements.txt
```

For Brotli compression (smaller files), install `pip install "whitenoise[brotli]"` instead.

### 19.2 Add the middleware — position matters

```python
MIDDLEWARE = [
    'django.middleware.security.SecurityMiddleware',
    'whitenoise.middleware.WhiteNoiseMiddleware',      # 👈 directly after SecurityMiddleware
    'django.contrib.sessions.middleware.SessionMiddleware',
    # ... the rest unchanged ...
]
```

It must be **above** everything except `SecurityMiddleware`, so static requests are answered before sessions, auth, `LoginRequiredMiddleware`, etc. run.

### 19.3 Use WhiteNoise's storage

```python
STORAGES = {
    'default': {
        'BACKEND': 'django.core.files.storage.FileSystemStorage',
    },
    'staticfiles': {
        'BACKEND': 'whitenoise.storage.CompressedManifestStaticFilesStorage',
    },
}
```

This is `ManifestStaticFilesStorage` (hashing, Step 16) **plus** compressed copies (`style.27e20196a850.css.gz`, `.br`). WhiteNoise sends the compressed version to browsers that support it, and sends hashed files with `Cache-Control: max-age=315360000, public, immutable` (cache for 10 years — safe, because the name changes when the content does).

### 19.4 Use WhiteNoise in development too (optional but recommended)

So development behaves like production, add `whitenoise.runserver_nostatic` **above** `django.contrib.staticfiles`:

```python
INSTALLED_APPS = [
    # ...
    'whitenoise.runserver_nostatic',   # 👈 must come before staticfiles
    'django.contrib.staticfiles',
    # ...
]
```

This disables Django's own `runserver` static handling, so WhiteNoise's middleware serves the files. With `DEBUG = True`, WhiteNoise looks at your **source** folders through the finders (`WHITENOISE_USE_FINDERS`) and picks up changes without restart (`WHITENOISE_AUTOREFRESH`) — both default to the value of `DEBUG`.

### 19.5 Useful WhiteNoise settings

| Setting                       | Default                     | Meaning                                                              |
|-------------------------------|-----------------------------|----------------------------------------------------------------------|
