| `WHITENOISE_MAX_AGE`          | 60 s (0 when `DEBUG`)       | Cache time for **non**-hashed files                                  |
| `WHITENOISE_USE_FINDERS`      | `DEBUG`                     | Serve from source folders instead of `STATIC_ROOT`                   |
| `WHITENOISE_AUTOREFRESH`      | `DEBUG`                     | Re-scan files on every request (slow — dev only)                     |
| `WHITENOISE_MANIFEST_STRICT`  | `True`                      | Same as `manifest_strict` (Step 16.6)                                |
| `WHITENOISE_KEEP_ONLY_HASHED_FILES` | `False`               | Delete unhashed originals from `STATIC_ROOT` after collecting        |
| `WHITENOISE_ROOT`             | `None`                      | A folder served at the site **root** — for `robots.txt`, `favicon.ico` |

### 19.6 Test a production setup locally on Windows (Waitress)

```bash
pip install waitress
```

In `settings.py` (temporarily, or via environment variables):

```python
DEBUG = False
ALLOWED_HOSTS = ['127.0.0.1', 'localhost']
```

```bash
python manage.py collectstatic --noinput --clear
waitress-serve --listen=127.0.0.1:8000 config.wsgi:application
```

Open **http://127.0.0.1:8000/**, view source — hashed URLs:

```html
<link rel="stylesheet" href="/static/blog/style.27e20196a850.css">
```

DevTools → Network → click the file → Response Headers:

```
Content-Type: text/css; charset="utf-8"
Cache-Control: max-age=315360000, public, immutable
Content-Encoding: gzip           (or br)
```

Open **http://127.0.0.1:8000/admin/** — styled. 🎉

Important: in production WhiteNoise scans `STATIC_ROOT` **once at startup**. Files collected after the server started aren't served until you restart it.

---

## Step 20: Serving with a Web Server (Nginx, Apache, IIS)

The web server answers `/static/` itself; everything else is forwarded to Django.

### 20.1 Nginx

```nginx
server {
    listen 80;
    server_name example.com;

    location /static/ {
        alias /srv/myproject/staticfiles/;         # STATIC_ROOT — note BOTH trailing slashes
        expires 1y;
        add_header Cache-Control "public, immutable";
        access_log off;
    }

    location /media/ {
        alias /srv/myproject/media/;               # MEDIA_ROOT (Step 22)
    }

    location / {
        proxy_pass http://127.0.0.1:8000;          # Gunicorn / Waitress
        proxy_set_header Host $host;
        proxy_set_header X-Forwarded-Proto $scheme;
    }
}
```

- `location /static/` must match `STATIC_URL`.
- Use `alias` (not `root`) with trailing slashes on both sides.
- `immutable` / 1-year caching is only safe with **hashed** file names (Step 16).
- The Nginx user (e.g. `www-data`) must be able to read `staticfiles/` (Step 14.10).

### 20.2 Apache (`mod_wsgi`)

```apache
Alias /static/ /srv/myproject/staticfiles/
<Directory /srv/myproject/staticfiles>
    Require all granted
</Directory>

WSGIScriptAlias / /srv/myproject/config/wsgi.py
```

The `Alias` must be defined so it's matched before `WSGIScriptAlias /`.

### 20.3 IIS (Windows Server)

Add a **Virtual Directory** named `static` pointing at the `staticfiles` folder, under the site that proxies to Django (via HttpPlatformHandler or wfastcgi). Make sure the static virtual directory is **not** handled by the Python handler (remove the handler mapping for that directory), so IIS serves files itself.

### 20.4 With a web server, do I still need WhiteNoise?

No — choose one. If Nginx serves `/static/`, Django (and WhiteNoise) never sees those requests. You can still use `ManifestStaticFilesStorage` for hashed names.

---

## Step 21: CDN and Cloud Storage

### 21.1 Just a CDN in front of your site

Simplest: keep WhiteNoise (or Nginx) and put a CDN (Cloudflare, CloudFront…) in front of the whole site. Or point `STATIC_URL` at a CDN that pulls from your site:

```python
STATIC_URL = 'https://cdn.example.com/static/'
```

`{% static %}` now returns `https://cdn.example.com/static/blog/style.27e20196a850.css`. The CDN fetches from `https://example.com/static/...` on first request and caches it. Notes:

- With a full URL in `STATIC_URL`, `runserver` won't serve static files — use this only in production settings.
- **Fonts** loaded cross-origin need a CORS header (`Access-Control-Allow-Origin`) on the CDN/origin.

### 21.2 Upload to S3 with `django-storages`

```bash
pip install "django-storages[s3]"
```

```python
STORAGES = {
    'default': {
        'BACKEND': 'django.core.files.storage.FileSystemStorage',
    },
    'staticfiles': {
        'BACKEND': 'storages.backends.s3.S3ManifestStaticStorage',   # S3 + hashing
        'OPTIONS': {
            'bucket_name': 'myblog-static',
            'location': 'static',            # folder inside the bucket
            'querystring_auth': False,       # public URLs without signatures
        },
    },
}
STATIC_URL = 'https://myblog-static.s3.amazonaws.com/static/'
```

Credentials come from environment variables (`AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID`, `AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY`) — never hard-code them. `collectstatic` now **uploads** to the bucket (slower than copying; only changed files are re-uploaded). `STATIC_ROOT` isn't used by this backend.

---

## Step 22: Media Files Are Not Static Files

### 22.1 Settings

```python
MEDIA_URL = 'media/'
MEDIA_ROOT = BASE_DIR / 'media'
```

- `MEDIA_URL` ≠ `STATIC_URL`, and `MEDIA_ROOT` ≠ `STATIC_ROOT` (Django raises `ImproperlyConfigured` otherwise).
- `MEDIA_ROOT` must not be inside `STATICFILES_DIRS` or `STATIC_ROOT`.

### 22.2 Serve media in development

`runserver` serves **static** files only — media needs a URL pattern:

```python
# config/urls.py
from django.conf import settings
from django.conf.urls.static import static as static_urls   # URL-pattern helper (Step 10.1)
from django.contrib import admin
from django.urls import include, path

urlpatterns = [
    path('admin/', admin.site.urls),
    path('', include('blog.urls')),
    # ...
]

if settings.DEBUG:
    urlpatterns += static_urls(settings.MEDIA_URL, document_root=settings.MEDIA_ROOT)
```

(`static_urls()` returns `[]` when `DEBUG = False` anyway; the `if` makes the intent obvious.) Add `media/` to `.gitignore`.

### 22.3 Why keep them apart

- Static files are **trusted** (you wrote them); uploads are **not** (a user can upload `evil.html` or `evil.svg` with scripts).
- `collectstatic --clear` deletes `STATIC_ROOT` — you'd lose every upload if they lived there.
- Static files can be cached forever; uploads change and may need permission checks.
- In production, serve media from a separate path / bucket, ideally a separate domain.

---

## Step 23: Front-End Build Tools (Sass, Tailwind, npm, Vite)

Django doesn't compile Sass, minify JS or bundle modules. Use a build tool that writes its **output** into a folder Django knows, then let staticfiles do the rest.

### 23.1 The pattern

```
assets/                       ← SOURCE you edit (not a static folder)
├── scss/main.scss
└── css/input.css
        │   npm run build / watch
        ▼
static/dist/                  ← OUTPUT, inside STATICFILES_DIRS
├── main.css
└── tailwind.css
        │   collectstatic
        ▼
staticfiles/dist/...          ← served in production
```

### 23.2 Sass

```bash
npm init -y
npm install --save-dev sass
npx sass assets/scss/main.scss static/dist/main.css --watch
```

```html
<link rel="stylesheet" href="{% static 'dist/main.css' %}">
```

### 23.3 Tailwind CSS (v4 CLI)

```bash
npm install --save-dev tailwindcss @tailwindcss/cli
```

`assets/css/input.css`:

```css
@import "tailwindcss";
@source "../../**/templates/**/*.html";
```

```bash
npx @tailwindcss/cli -i ./assets/css/input.css -o ./static/dist/tailwind.css --watch
```

Run the watcher in a second terminal next to `runserver`.

### 23.4 Rules

- Never add `node_modules` itself to `STATICFILES_DIRS` (thousands of files would be collected and made public). Expose single package folders with a prefix (Step 7.4) or let the bundler copy what you need.
- Decide if `static/dist/` is committed or built during deploy. If built during deploy, add it to `.gitignore` and run the build **before** `collectstatic`.
- If the bundler already adds hashes to file names, you can still use `ManifestStaticFilesStorage` (double hashing is harmless) — or use a helper package like `django-vite` that reads the bundler's own manifest.
- Exclude source files from collection (`--ignore "*.scss"` or Step 14.8).

---

## Step 24: Absolute URLs, Emails and Sub-Path Deployments

### 24.1 Absolute URLs (emails, Open Graph, RSS)

`{% static %}` returns `/static/...` — fine in a browser, useless in an **email** (no domain). Make it absolute:

```python
# in a view
from django.templatetags.static import static

logo_url = request.build_absolute_uri(static('blog/images/logo.svg'))
# 'http://127.0.0.1:8000/static/blog/images/logo.svg'
```

Outside a request (management commands, background tasks), keep the site's base URL in settings:

```python
# config/settings.py
SITE_URL = 'https://example.com'
```

```python
from django.conf import settings
from django.templatetags.static import static

logo_url = f'{settings.SITE_URL}{static("blog/images/logo.svg")}'
```

If `STATIC_URL` is already a full CDN URL, `static()` is already absolute — check with `urllib.parse.urlsplit(url).netloc` before prefixing.

Note: many email clients block or strip SVG — use PNG for email images.

### 24.2 Deploying under a sub-path

If the site lives at `https://example.com/myblog/`, the WSGI server sets `SCRIPT_NAME = '/myblog'` (or you set `FORCE_SCRIPT_NAME = '/myblog'`). A **relative** `STATIC_URL = 'static/'` then automatically becomes `/myblog/static/`. An absolute `STATIC_URL = '/static/'` would not — another reason to keep the default relative form.

---

## Step 25: Test Static Files

### 25.1 Finders and URLs

```python
# blog/tests.py
from django.contrib.staticfiles import finders
from django.template import Context, Template
from django.templatetags.static import static
from django.test import SimpleTestCase, TestCase
from django.urls import reverse


class StaticFilesTests(SimpleTestCase):
    def test_blog_css_exists(self):
        self.assertIsNotNone(finders.find('blog/style.css'))

    def test_project_css_exists(self):
        self.assertIsNotNone(finders.find('css/base.css'))

    def test_static_helper(self):
        self.assertEqual(static('blog/style.css'), '/static/blog/style.css')

    def test_static_tag(self):
        html = Template("{% load static %}{% static 'blog/style.css' %}").render(Context())
        self.assertEqual(html, '/static/blog/style.css')


class BaseTemplateStaticTests(TestCase):
    def test_post_list_links_stylesheets(self):
        response = self.client.get(reverse('blog:post_list'))
        self.assertContains(response, 'href="/static/css/base.css"')
        self.assertContains(response, 'href="/static/blog/style.css"')
```

`SimpleTestCase` is enough when no database is needed.

### 25.2 Make sure every `{% static %}` file exists

A test that walks all templates and checks every referenced file catches typos before production does:

```python
import re
from pathlib import Path

from django.conf import settings
from django.contrib.staticfiles import finders
from django.test import SimpleTestCase

STATIC_TAG = re.compile(r"""{%\s*static\s+['"]([^'"]+)['"]""")


class AllStaticReferencesExistTests(SimpleTestCase):
    def test_every_static_reference_exists(self):
        missing = []
        for template in Path(settings.BASE_DIR).glob('**/templates/**/*.html'):
            if 'venv' in template.parts:
                continue
            for path in STATIC_TAG.findall(template.read_text(encoding='utf-8')):
                if finders.find(path) is None:
                    missing.append(f'{template}: {path}')
        self.assertEqual(missing, [])
```

### 25.3 `ManifestStaticFilesStorage` in tests

The test runner always uses `DEBUG = False`, so with manifest storage every page that uses `{% static %}` fails with `ValueError: Missing staticfiles manifest entry ...` unless you ran `collectstatic`. Use the plain storage when testing:

```python
# config/settings.py (at the bottom)
import sys

TESTING = len(sys.argv) > 1 and sys.argv[1] == 'test'

if TESTING:
    STORAGES['staticfiles']['BACKEND'] = 'django.contrib.staticfiles.storage.StaticFilesStorage'
```

### 25.4 Test `collectstatic` and hashing

```python
import tempfile
from pathlib import Path

from django.contrib.staticfiles.storage import staticfiles_storage
from django.core.management import call_command
from django.test import SimpleTestCase, override_settings


class CollectStaticTests(SimpleTestCase):
    def test_collectstatic_with_manifest(self):
        with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as tmp:
            storages = {
                'default': {'BACKEND': 'django.core.files.storage.FileSystemStorage'},
                'staticfiles': {'BACKEND': 'django.contrib.staticfiles.storage.ManifestStaticFilesStorage'},
            }
            with override_settings(STATIC_ROOT=tmp, STORAGES=storages):
                call_command('collectstatic', interactive=False, verbosity=0)

                self.assertTrue((Path(tmp) / 'staticfiles.json').exists())
                self.assertRegex(
                    staticfiles_storage.url('blog/style.css'),
                    r'^/static/blog/style\.[0-9a-f]{12}\.css$',
                )
```

`override_settings` of `STATIC_ROOT` / `STORAGES` resets `staticfiles_storage` automatically. `interactive=False` is the Python equivalent of `--noinput`. A temp folder keeps your real `staticfiles/` untouched.

### 25.5 `StaticLiveServerTestCase`

`LiveServerTestCase` starts a real server for browser tests (Selenium, Playwright) but does **not** serve static files from your source folders. `StaticLiveServerTestCase` does (through the finders, like `runserver`):

```python
from urllib.request import urlopen

from django.contrib.staticfiles.testing import StaticLiveServerTestCase
from django.templatetags.static import static


class LiveStaticTests(StaticLiveServerTestCase):
    def test_css_is_served(self):
        with urlopen(self.live_server_url + static('blog/style.css')) as response:
            self.assertEqual(response.status, 200)
            self.assertIn('text/css', response.headers['Content-Type'])
```

### 25.6 Run the tests

```bash
python manage.py test blog
```

---

## Step 26: Security

- **Everything in `STATIC_ROOT` is public.** Never put secrets, private documents, `.env` files, or source code in static folders. (The default `.*` ignore pattern skips dotfiles, but don't rely on it.)
- **Never let users upload into static folders.** Uploads are media (Step 22), served separately.
- **`STATIC_ROOT` must not contain your code** (e.g. `STATIC_ROOT = BASE_DIR`) — the web server would publish `settings.py`.
- **Don't run `runserver --insecure` in production** (or `runserver` at all in production).
- **Delete stale files**: renamed/deleted source files stay public in `STATIC_ROOT` until `collectstatic --clear`.
- **Third-party scripts from CDNs**: pin exact versions and use Subresource Integrity:
  ```html
  <script src="https://cdn.example.com/lib@1.2.3/lib.min.js"
          integrity="sha384-..." crossorigin="anonymous" defer></script>
  ```
  Or vendor the file into `static/vendor/` so you serve it yourself.
- **Content-Security-Policy**: keeping JavaScript in static files (not inline `<script>` blocks or `onclick=` attributes) lets you use a strict CSP like `script-src 'self'`. Django 6.0+ has built-in CSP support (`SECURE_CSP`); older versions use the `django-csp` package.
- **SVG files can contain scripts.** Your own SVGs are fine; never serve user-uploaded SVGs from your main domain.

---

## Step 27: Performance and Caching

1. **Hashed names + long cache** — `ManifestStaticFilesStorage` (or WhiteNoise's version) and `Cache-Control: public, max-age=31536000, immutable`. Returning visitors download nothing.
2. **Compression** — WhiteNoise's `CompressedManifestStaticFilesStorage` (gzip + Brotli), or `gzip on;` / `brotli on;` in Nginx. CSS/JS shrink 70–80%.
3. **Don't serve static through Django views** — use WhiteNoise, a web server or a CDN.
4. **Load JS with `defer`** or `type="module"`; put CSS in `<head>`.
5. **Preload critical fonts**:
   ```html
   <link rel="preload" href="{% static 'fonts/inter.woff2' %}" as="font" type="font/woff2" crossorigin>
   ```
6. **Optimise images** — modern formats (WebP/AVIF), correct dimensions, `loading="lazy"` for images below the fold.
7. **Minify / bundle** with a build tool (Step 23) — Django doesn't minify.
8. **Fewer, smaller files** — remove unused CSS/JS (Tailwind does this automatically).

Check results in DevTools → **Network** (sizes, `304`s, `(disk cache)`) and **Lighthouse**.

---

## Step 28: Production Checklist

- [ ] `django.contrib.staticfiles` in `INSTALLED_APPS`.
- [ ] `STATIC_URL = 'static/'` (or your CDN URL), ending in a slash.
- [ ] `STATIC_ROOT` set to a dedicated folder (not in `STATICFILES_DIRS`, not `BASE_DIR`, not `MEDIA_ROOT`).
- [ ] `STATICFILES_DIRS` lists only real source folders; `python manage.py check` shows no `staticfiles.*` issues.
- [ ] App files namespaced: `<app>/static/<app>/...`.
- [ ] Templates use `{% static %}` everywhere — no hard-coded `/static/`; CSS uses relative `url()`s.
- [ ] `STORAGES['staticfiles']` = `ManifestStaticFilesStorage` or `whitenoise.storage.CompressedManifestStaticFilesStorage` (and `STORAGES['default']` still defined).
- [ ] Tests use the plain storage (Step 25.3).
- [ ] Deploy runs `python manage.py collectstatic --noinput` (plus `--clear` when files were removed) **before** restarting the app server.
- [ ] Something serves `STATIC_ROOT`: WhiteNoise middleware (right after `SecurityMiddleware`), Nginx/Apache/IIS, or a CDN.
- [ ] Long cache headers on hashed files; compression on.
- [ ] Admin pages are styled in production (quick smoke test).
- [ ] `staticfiles/`, `media/`, `node_modules/` in `.gitignore`.
- [ ] No secrets or user uploads in static folders.

---

## Reference: Settings

| Setting                 | Default                                                     | Meaning                                                                         |
|-------------------------|-------------------------------------------------------------|---------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| `STATIC_URL`            | `None` (`startproject` sets `'static/'`)                    | URL prefix for static files; must end with `/`; relative values get the script prefix |
| `STATIC_ROOT`           | `None`                                                      | Absolute folder `collectstatic` copies into                                     |
| `STATICFILES_DIRS`      | `[]`                                                        | Extra source folders (paths or `(prefix, path)` tuples)                         |
| `STATICFILES_FINDERS`   | `FileSystemFinder`, `AppDirectoriesFinder`                  | Finder classes, searched in order                                               |
| `STORAGES['staticfiles']` | `{'BACKEND': 'django.contrib.staticfiles.storage.StaticFilesStorage'}` | Storage used by `collectstatic` and `{% static %}`              |
| `STATICFILES_STORAGE`   | —                                                           | **Removed in Django 5.1** — use `STORAGES`                                      |
| `FILE_UPLOAD_PERMISSIONS` | `0o644`                                                   | Permissions of collected files (local storage)                                  |
| `FILE_UPLOAD_DIRECTORY_PERMISSIONS` | `None`                                          | Permissions of created folders                                                  |
| `DEBUG`                 | `False`                                                     | `True` → `runserver` serves static, manifest storage returns unhashed URLs      |
| `FORCE_SCRIPT_NAME`     | `None`                                                      | Overrides the script prefix added to a relative `STATIC_URL`                    |
| `MEDIA_URL` / `MEDIA_ROOT` | `''`                                                     | Uploads — must differ from `STATIC_URL` / `STATIC_ROOT`                         |

## Reference: Template Tags (`{% load static %}`)

| Tag                                    | Output                                        |
|----------------------------------------|-----------------------------------------------|
| `{% static 'path' %}`                  | URL for the static path (via the storage)     |
| `{% static 'path' as var %}`           | Stores the URL in `var`                        |
| `{% static some_variable %}`           | Path taken from a variable                    |
| `{% get_static_prefix %}` / `as var`   | `STATIC_URL`                                  |
| `{% get_media_prefix %}` / `as var`    | `MEDIA_URL`                                   |
| `{{ STATIC_URL }}`                     | Needs `django.template.context_processors.static` |
| `{{ form.media }}` / `.css` / `.js`    | Tags for a form's/widget's `Media`            |

## Reference: Management Commands

| Command                                | Main options                                                                                   |
|----------------------------------------|------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| `collectstatic`                        | `--noinput`, `--clear`/`-c`, `--dry-run`/`-n`, `--link`/`-l`, `--ignore`/`-i`, `--no-default-ignore`, `--no-post-process`, `-v` |
| `findstatic <path> [<path> ...]`       | `--first`, `-v 0/1/2`                                                                          |
| `runserver`                            | `--nostatic`, `--insecure` (plus all normal `runserver` options)                               |

## Reference: Python API

| Import                                                               | Use                                                               |
|----------------------------------------------------------------------|-------------------------------------------------------------------|
| `from django.templatetags.static import static`                      | `static(path)` → URL                                              |
| `from django.contrib.staticfiles.storage import staticfiles_storage` | `.url()`, `.path()`, `.exists()`, `.open()` on collected files    |
| `from django.contrib.staticfiles import finders`                     | `finders.find(path, find_all=False)`, `finders.searched_locations`, `finders.get_finders()` |
| `from django.contrib.staticfiles.finders import BaseFinder`          | Base class for custom finders: `find()`, `list()`, `check()`      |
| `from django.contrib.staticfiles.storage import ManifestStaticFilesStorage, StaticFilesStorage, ManifestFilesMixin, HashedFilesMixin` | Storage classes to use or subclass |
| `from django.contrib.staticfiles.utils import get_files, matches_patterns` | Helpers for custom finders/storages                          |
| `from django.contrib.staticfiles.views import serve`                 | Dev view: `serve(request, path, insecure=False)`                  |
| `from django.contrib.staticfiles.urls import staticfiles_urlpatterns`| Dev URL patterns for the `serve` view                             |
| `from django.contrib.staticfiles.handlers import StaticFilesHandler, ASGIStaticFilesHandler` | WSGI/ASGI wrappers that serve static files |
| `from django.contrib.staticfiles.testing import StaticLiveServerTestCase` | Live-server tests with static files                          |
| `from django.contrib.staticfiles.apps import StaticFilesConfig`      | Subclass to change `ignore_patterns`                              |
| `from django.conf.urls.static import static`                         | **Different function**: dev URL patterns (for media)              |

## Reference: Errors and System Checks

| Message                                                                                         | Meaning / fix                                                        |
|-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|----------------------------------------------------------------------|
| `staticfiles.E001` STATICFILES_DIRS is not a tuple or list                                      | Use a list; watch for a missing trailing comma in tuples              |
| `staticfiles.E002` STATICFILES_DIRS should not contain STATIC_ROOT                               | Use a different folder for `STATIC_ROOT`                              |
| `staticfiles.E003` prefix ... must not end with a slash                                          | `('downloads', ...)`, not `('downloads/', ...)`                       |
| `staticfiles.W004` directory ... does not exist                                                  | Create it or fix the path                                             |
| `staticfiles.E005` STORAGES must define a 'staticfiles' storage                                  | Add the `'staticfiles'` key                                           |
| `ImproperlyConfigured: ... without having set the required STATIC_URL setting`                   | Set `STATIC_URL`                                                      |
| `ImproperlyConfigured: ... without having set the STATIC_ROOT setting to a filesystem path`      | Set `STATIC_ROOT` before `collectstatic`                              |
| `ImproperlyConfigured: The MEDIA_URL and STATIC_URL settings must have different values`         | Change one                                                            |
| `ValueError: Missing staticfiles manifest entry for '...'`                                       | Typo, leading slash, `collectstatic` not run, or tests with manifest storage |
| `Post-processing '...' failed!` + `The file '...' could not be found with <...Storage...>`       | A CSS file references a missing file (often a `.map`)                 |
| `Max post-process passes exceeded.`                                                              | Circular references between CSS/JS files                              |
| `Found another file with the destination path '...'`                                             | Two files with the same static path — namespace them                  |
| `TemplateSyntaxError: Invalid block tag ... 'static'`                                            | Add `{% load static %}` to that template                              |
| `OSError: [WinError 1314] A required privilege is not held by the client`                        | `collectstatic --link` on Windows without Developer Mode / admin      |

---

## Troubleshooting

| Problem                                                    | Check / fix                                                                                                      |
|------------------------------------------------------------|------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| CSS/JS 404 in development                                  | `findstatic <path> -v 2`; app in `INSTALLED_APPS`? folder named exactly `static`? namespaced path correct? restarted `runserver` after creating the folder? |
| Everything 404s, page unstyled                             | `DEBUG = False` with `runserver` → expected. Use `DEBUG = True`, or WhiteNoise                                   |
| Changes to CSS don't show                                  | Hard refresh (`Ctrl+F5`), DevTools "Disable cache", or another file with the same path wins (`findstatic`)        |
| Admin is unstyled in production                            | `collectstatic` not run, or nothing serves `STATIC_ROOT` (Step 18)                                               |
| 500 error in production, `Missing staticfiles manifest entry` | Run `collectstatic`; fix typos/leading slashes; restart the server after collecting                            |
| Tests fail with `Missing staticfiles manifest entry`       | Use `StaticFilesStorage` in tests (Step 25.3)                                                                     |
| `collectstatic` fails with post-processing error           | Missing file referenced from CSS — often a `.map` (Step 16.7)                                                    |
| Images in CSS 404 in production but not in dev             | Absolute `/static/...` in CSS, or wrong relative path; use paths relative to the CSS file                        |
| Wrong file served                                          | Same static path in two places — `findstatic` shows both; namespace or reorder                                   |
| Deleted file still downloadable                            | `collectstatic --clear`                                                                                          |
| Browser: "Refused to apply style ... MIME type ('text/plain')" | Windows registry MIME types — Step 13.8                                                                      |
| Fonts from CDN blocked (CORS error in console)             | Add `Access-Control-Allow-Origin` on the CDN/origin                                                               |
| Hashed URLs 404 with `runserver --insecure`                | Expected — `--insecure` serves source folders; test with WhiteNoise + Waitress (Step 19.6)                        |
| New files 404 with WhiteNoise in production                | WhiteNoise scans at startup — restart after `collectstatic`                                                      |
| File uploads broke after adding `STORAGES`                 | You removed the `'default'` key — define both                                                                    |
| `STATICFILES_STORAGE` setting ignored / error              | Removed in Django 5.1 — move it to `STORAGES['staticfiles']`                                                     |

## Quick Reference

```python
# settings.py
INSTALLED_APPS = [..., 'whitenoise.runserver_nostatic', 'django.contrib.staticfiles', ...]
MIDDLEWARE = [
    'django.middleware.security.SecurityMiddleware',
    'whitenoise.middleware.WhiteNoiseMiddleware',       # right after SecurityMiddleware
    ...,
]
STATIC_URL = 'static/'
STATIC_ROOT = BASE_DIR / 'staticfiles'
STATICFILES_DIRS = [BASE_DIR / 'static']
STORAGES = {
    'default': {'BACKEND': 'django.core.files.storage.FileSystemStorage'},
    'staticfiles': {'BACKEND': 'whitenoise.storage.CompressedManifestStaticFilesStorage'},
    # or 'django.contrib.staticfiles.storage.ManifestStaticFilesStorage'
}
MEDIA_URL = 'media/'
MEDIA_ROOT = BASE_DIR / 'media'

# Python
from django.templatetags.static import static
static('blog/style.css')                                   # URL
from django.contrib.staticfiles import finders
finders.find('blog/style.css')                             # source file on disk
from django.contrib.staticfiles.storage import staticfiles_storage
staticfiles_storage.url('blog/style.css')                  # same as static()
request.build_absolute_uri(static('blog/images/logo.svg')) # absolute URL

# forms
class Media:
    css = {'all': ['blog/widgets/markdown.css']}
    js = ['blog/widgets/markdown.js']
```

```html
{% load static %}
<link rel="stylesheet" href="{% static 'blog/style.css' %}">
<script src="{% static 'blog/js/post.js' %}" defer></script>
<img src="{% static 'blog/images/logo.svg' %}" alt="Logo">
{% static 'blog/images/logo.svg' as logo_url %}
{{ form.media }}
```

```css
/* inside CSS: relative to the CSS file */
background-image: url("../images/pattern.svg");
```

```bash
python manage.py findstatic blog/style.css -v 2        # where is it?
python manage.py collectstatic --noinput               # deploy
python manage.py collectstatic --noinput --clear       # deploy, removing stale files
python manage.py collectstatic --dry-run -v 2          # preview
python manage.py runserver --nostatic                  # don't serve static
python manage.py runserver --insecure                  # serve static with DEBUG=False (local only)
```
